items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: The fellow by the name of Art Stewart, that was a conductor... I'd go and rehearse with him every Sunday.

ctx.x: Doc Willow? Yeah. Yeah. And Raymond Valentine. And we had Cass Simpson on piano and accordion. And we had Boris Lovingood. He's from, I think Austin, Texas. And we had the, we had the, five brass. And I think we had four reeds. Two pianists and Snagg Jones on the drum. So we had a battle with this, the same McKinney's Cotspickers. Don Redman had them then, you heard of Don Redman had them. So they were working out of this Greystone ballroom in Detroit. So they were booked there. We played the Matinee on Sunday…
Who was this guy, Percy, you were saying? I guess it was back at Bill Bottoms or something.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I must attribute my success, what success I had, Art Stewart, the big K.P. band... He always hollering at me, get in there!

ctx.x: Well I wanted to play the clarinet.

Did you ever get the clarinet at all? That's why it'd take me so long with the trombone, see. No, never did, nothing but the trombone. After I began to play it and people would take notes and I'd say well I'd just go ahead on through with it. I'm glad I did now. Because they told me, he says, there isn't but a few, at that time you didn't have the musicians they have now, everywhere you look, he says there ain't but a few good trombone players around here. And I held the top up top there around here, not…
I talked to him the other day.
